name: Tacrolimus
route_note: oral capsules twice daily or extended-release once daily; IV infusion; 0.03–0.1% ointment for atopic dermatitis

discovery.by: Fujisawa researchers (Toshio Goto, Toru Kino and colleagues)
discovery.note: Isolated from Streptomyces tsukubaensis in a soil sample from Tsukuba, Japan; about 10–100 times more potent than ciclosporin in vitro.

tagline: Potent macrolide calcineurin inhibitor at the core of transplant immunosuppression
summary: Tacrolimus is a macrolide from Streptomyces tsukubaensis that inhibits calcineurin after binding FKBP12, blocking T-cell activation. It is the most widely used calcineurin inhibitor for preventing rejection after kidney, liver and heart transplantation, and a topical form treats atopic dermatitis. It has a narrow therapeutic window and needs blood-level monitoring.
mechanism: Tacrolimus enters T cells and binds the immunophilin FKBP12. The tacrolimus–FKBP12 complex inhibits the phosphatase calcineurin, preventing dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation of NFAT transcription factors.

As a result, transcription of interleukin-2, interferon-gamma and other cytokines is suppressed and T-cell proliferation in response to alloantigens is blocked. The mechanism resembles ciclosporin's but uses a different immunophilin and is more potent per milligram.
uses: Prophylaxis of organ rejection in kidney, liver, heart and lung transplantation
Treatment of rejection resistant to other immunosuppressants

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Fujisawa isolates FK506 from a Japanese soil actinomycete.

history.title: Pittsburgh trials
history.detail: Thomas Starzl's team reports rescue of liver transplant recipients with FK506.

history.title: Japanese approval
history.detail: Prograf approved in Japan for liver transplantation.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Prograf for liver transplantation; kidney approval follows in 1997.

history.title: Protopic
history.detail: Tacrolimus ointment approved for atopic dermatitis.

history.title: Topical boxed warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning on theoretical malignancy risk to topical calcineurin inhibitors.

history.title: Extended release
history.detail: Once-daily Advagraf authorised in the EU; similar products follow in the US (Astagraf XL 2013, Envarsus XR 2015).

pk.half_life: about 12 hours in transplant patients (longer in healthy volunteers)

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of serious infections and malignancies such as lymphoma; prescribe only where experienced in immunosuppression. Extended-release forms carry warnings on mortality in female liver transplant recipients (Astagraf XL).

facts: Carriers of a functional CYP3A5 allele, more common in people of African ancestry, often need higher doses to reach target blood levels.
Its name combines Tsukuba, macrolide and immunosuppressant.
